beats.title: Call to order — the agenda
beats.shows: the CEO opens the meeting and frames the cross-functional question
beats.question: Call the C-suite meeting to order. Agenda: state of the bank this week. Do NOT consult any officer yet — that happens later, round the table. Right now just open the meeting and state, in one line each, the question you will put to the CFO, COO, CTO and CXO. This is a framing statement, not a report — open it the way a chair actually would: confident and plain, in command of the room.
beats.answer:
Good morning. Let’s call this to order.

**CFO:** Walk us through the books—profitability, NIM, RAROC and capital position this week. What’s changed and where are we exposed?

**COO:** Give us the state of money-movement—rails, settlement, float and any operational incidents or near-misses. Are we clean or are we carrying risk into the weekend?

**CTO:** Report platform health—reliability, deployments, open incidents and technical debt. Is the stack stable or are we flying blind?

**CXO:** Bring the customer voice—onboarding friction, NPS, CSAT and any spikes in complaints or attrition signals. What are customers actually feeling right now?

We’ll go round the table. CFO, you’re first.

beats.title: Round the table — CFO + COO
beats.shows: the CEO consults the finance + operations seats; figures attributed
beats.question: Go round the table. First the CFO: what do the books say this week (profitability / NIM / capital)? Then the COO: how are the payment rails and settlement running? Attribute every figure.
beats.answer:
Thank you, CFO. Thank you, COO. Here is what I’m hearing so far.

---

**CFO — the books:**

The CFO reports the latest close is **September 2026**, with August as the prior period. Net income fell to **CAD 1,646.44**, down from **CAD 3,292.88** in August—a 50% drop month-over-month. ROA annualized is now **0.13%**, down from **0.27%**; ROE annualized is **1.34%**, down from **2.58%**.

NIM is the headline problem. The CFO reports it collapsed to **0%** in August and stayed at **0%** in September, against **2.10%** in July. Interest income and interest expense are both booked at zero despite **CAD 8,294,115.625** in average earning assets in September.

RAROC is deeply negative: **–11.11%** in September, from **–9.13%** in August and **+0.15%** in July. Expected loss for September is **CAD 10,654.14**, and economic profit is **–CAD 109,593.66**. The CFO notes the ledger books **no loan-loss provision**, so the headline ROA/ROE look better than true economics.

Capital is razor-thin. Total equity is **CAD 1,515,656.15**, but the leverage ratio is **0.10%** and the RWA capital ratio is **0.15%**—both essentially unchanged and far below prudential norms. Total assets grew by **CAD 317,798.13** to **CAD 14,843,055.22**, which diluted the ratios further.

Credit exposure stands at **CAD 8,320,845.29**, with the loan-to-deposit ratio at **5.96x**. Segment reporting is broken: September shows only one segment (`card|payments` at CAD 801.94) with an unreconciled variance of **–CAD 844.50** against the GL.

The CFO’s bottom line: the bank is pre-provision profitable but economically loss-making, with the interest engine switched off and fee revenue halved.

---

**COO — operations and rails:**

The COO reports over the **7-day window**, total transaction volume was **10,063 items for $2,194,926.74**. Interac is active: **768 e-Transfers deposited for $118,861.52**. AFT and Lynx recorded **zero transactions** and **$0** in the 7-day window.

The card rail is running. There were **2,104 captured purchases for $213,837.32** from **100 active cardholders** (plus 4 single-purchase), with **16 open authorization holds** totaling **$16,113.03**. The **7-day authorization approval rate is 89.91%**, with a **decline rate of 10.09%** and an **NSF rate of 10.09%**. Total 7-day declines: **312 items for $106,386.64**—**236 NSF declines on card_authorize ($73,963.96)** and **76 limit declines on withdrawals ($32,422.68)**.

Float is **–$12,528,415.55** point-in-time, which the COO explains reflects ordinary revolving intraday timing and deliberate overdraft capacity on rail system accounts, not a liquidity shortfall.

No operational incidents in the 7-day window—**zero exceptions** across failed transactions, reversals, returned AFT, rejected AFT, and wire recalls.

But the **30-day picture carries risk**. The COO reports **14 exceptions**: **4 reversals**, **6 rejected AFT entries ($243.00)**, and **4 wire recalls**. Most critically, the **Lynx rail** over 30 days shows a **25.00% recall rate by count** and **29.62% by value**—**$4,399,756.24 recalled** out of **$14,855,863.95** total Lynx volume. The 30-day AFT rail also shows **6 rejected entries ($243.00)** against **37 settled ($407,700.72)**.

Risks into the weekend: the persistent Lynx recall pattern, the **10.09% card NSF rate** signaling customer balance stress, and **16 ageing authorization holds ($16,113.03)** that could expire or capture unpredictably.

---

**Cross-functional note so far:** We have a bank with zero NIM, halved fee revenue, a **0.10%** leverage ratio, and a **25.00%** Lynx recall rate. That is not a stable equilibrium.

We still need to hear from the **CTO** and the **CXO**. CTO, you’re next—platform health and delivery. Then CXO will bring the customer voice.

Over the **7-day window**, nano-bank’s payment rails have reactivated significantly after a prior period of dormancy. Total transaction volume was **10,063 items for $2,194,926.74**. The Interac rail is running: **768 e-Transfers deposited for $118,861.52**. The AFT and Lynx rails were quiet, recording **zero transactions** and **$0** in the 7-day window.

The card rail is active. There were **2,104 captured purchases for $213,837.32** from **100 active cardholders** (plus **4 single-purchase cardholders**), with **16 open authorization holds** totaling **$16,113.03** as of the latest point-in-time snapshot. The **7-day authorization approval rate is 89.91%**, with **236 declines** out of **2,340 total attempts**, producing a **decline rate of 10.09%** and an **NSF rate of 10.09%**. Total **7-day declines** were **312 items for $106,386.64**, comprising **236 NSF declines on card_authorize ($73,963.96)** and **76 limit declines on withdrawals ($32,422.68)**.

The current **float position** is a point-in-time snapshot of **-$12,528,415.55**, with system-account components of **AFT -$394,355.12**, **cash -$1,395,876.29**, **Interac $13,912.20**, **Lynx -$10,441,107.71**, and **system -$310,988.63**. Under the bank’s clearing convention these negative balances reflect ordinary revolving intraday timing and deliberate overdraft capacity on the rail system accounts; they are **not** an indication of missing cash or a liquidity shortfall.

**Operational incidents in the 7-day window are absent.** Exceptions totaled **zero** across failed transactions, reversals, returned AFT entries, rejected AFT entries, and wire recalls.

However, **30-day data reveals carry-over risks**. Over **30 days**, there were **14 exceptions**: **4 reversals**, **6 rejected AFT entries ($243.00)**, and **4 wire recalls**. The **Lynx rail** over **30 days** shows a critically elevated recall rate of **25.00% by count** and **29.62% by value**, with **$4,399,756.24 recalled** out of **$14,855,863.95** in total Lynx volume. The **30-day AFT rail** also shows **6 rejected entries ($243.00)** against **37 settled ($407,700.72)**.

**Risks carrying into the weekend** include the persistent **Lynx recall pattern**, the **10.09% card NSF rate** indicating customer balance stress, and **16 ageing open authorization holds ($16,113.03)** that could expire or capture unpredictably. Additionally, while the **AFT rail** was dormant in the **7-day window**, the **30-day rejected-entry pattern** and prior batch-accumulator blockage remain unresolved technical concerns should outbound AFT volume resume.

Here is what the books say. The ledger only closes monthly, so "this week" is not available — the latest snapshot is **September 2026 (30-day period)**, with **August 2026** as the prior period for comparison. I also pulled **July 2026** to show the trend in NIM.

---

### 1. Profitability (pre-provision)

| Metric | Sep 2026 | Aug 2026 | Change |
|--------|----------|----------|--------|
| Net income | CAD 1,646.44 | CAD 3,292.88 | **–CAD 1,646.44** |
| ROA (annualized) | 0.13% | 0.27% | **–0.13 pp** |
| ROE (annualized) | 1.34% | 2.58% | **–1.25 pp** |
| Efficiency ratio | 0% | 0% | — |

**What it means:** Revenue collapsed by half month-over-month. The bank is still pre-provision profitable, but the trajectory is sharply negative. The efficiency ratio at 0% is artificial — there are no operating expenses booked in the GL, which is unrealistic and suggests incomplete cost capture.

---

### 2. Net Interest Margin (NIM)

| Period | Net Interest | Avg Earning Assets | NIM (annualized) |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Jul 2026 | CAD 7,287.58 | CAD 4,080,233.65 | **2.10%** |
| Aug 2026 | CAD 0.00 | CAD 8,213,926.63 | **0%** |
| Sep 2026 | CAD 0.00 | CAD 8,294,115.625 | **0%** |

**What it means:** NIM collapsed to zero in August and stayed there in September. Both interest income and interest expense are booked at CAD 0.00. This is the single biggest driver of the profitability decline — the bank is no longer earning any spread on its assets.

---

### 3. RAROC (Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital)

| Metric | Sep 2026 | Aug 2026 | Jul 2026 |
|--------|----------|----------|----------|
| RAROC (annualized) | **–11.11%** | **–9.13%** | +0.15% |
| Expected loss (period) | CAD 10,654.14 | CAD 10,873.06 | CAD 10,600.64 |
| Net income (annualized) | CAD 20,031.69 | CAD 38,771.01 | CAD 126,182.03 |
| Economic profit | –CAD 109,593.66 | –CAD 89,250.56 | +CAD 1,368.03 |

**What it means:** RAROC has deteriorated from barely positive in July to deeply negative. The bank's expected credit cost (~CAD 10,600 per month) now far exceeds its entire income. The ledger books **no loan-loss provision**, so ROA/ROE look better than the true economics; RAROC reveals the bank is destroying value after credit risk.

---

### 4. Capital Position

| Metric | Sep 2026 | Aug 2026 | Change |
|--------|----------|----------|--------|
| Total equity | CAD 1,515,656.15 | CAD 1,514,009.71 | +CAD 1,646.44 |
| Leverage ratio | 0.10% | 0.10% | **–0.002 pp** |
| RWA capital ratio | 0.15% | 0.15% | **–0.001 pp** |
| Total assets | CAD 14,843,055.22 | CAD 14,525,257.09 | +CAD 317,798.13 |

**What it means:** Capital remains **critically thin**. The leverage ratio is ~10 basis points and the RWA ratio ~15 basis points — far below any prudential standard. The bank is essentially running on a sliver of equity. The slight dip in ratios despite earnings is because assets grew faster than capital.

---

### 5. What Has Changed

- **Revenue halved:** Fee and interchange income dropped from CAD 3,292.88 to CAD 1,646.44. The ledger shows this as a clean 50% reduction — I cannot see why from the GL; the operational tables may hold the answer.
- **NIM remains dead:** Zero interest income for two consecutive months. This is not a one-off; the interest engine is switched off.
- **Asset growth without income:** Assets grew by CAD 317,798.13 (mainly Bank balances + Card receivables + deposits), but this growth is not generating revenue.
- **Segment reporting is broken:** In September, only one segment (`card|payments`, CAD 801.94) appears, with an unreconciled variance of **CAD –844.50** vs the GL. In August, the variance was **CAD –4,848.12**. The operational and GL populations are not aligned, so I cannot use segments to identify exposure concentrations.

---

### 6. Where We Are Exposed

**What the ledger CAN show:**

- **Credit exposure:** CAD 8,320,845.29 point-in-time. The bulk is:
  - **LoansReceivable:** CAD 8,000,001.00 (100% risk weight)
  - **Receivable:** CAD 402,982.66 (100% risk weight)
  - **CardReceivable:** CAD 320,844.29 (75% risk weight)
  - **Bank:** CAD 6,114,043.16 (20% risk weight)
- **Expected loss rate:** ~1.56% annualized — this is a heavy drag relative to income.
- **Loan-to-deposit ratio:** 5.96x (down from 7.66x in August, but still extreme). The bank is funding loans largely through non-deposit liabilities (Payables at CAD 11,925,333.21).

**What the ledger CANNOT show:**

- Liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) or HQLA buffers
- Concentration limits by counterparty, sector, or geography
- Asset maturities or repricing gaps
- Non-performing loans or delinquency rates
- Market risk or interest-rate risk in the banking book
- Operational loss events

---

### Bottom Line

The bank is **pre-provision profitable but economically loss-making**. NIM has collapsed to zero, fee revenue has halved, and credit risk costs consume more than the bank earns. Capital is at razor-thin levels (~10 bps leverage). The most urgent exposures are:
1. **Interest income failure** — why are we booking zero interest on CAD 8M+ in loans and receivables?
2. **Revenue concentration and decline** — half of fee/interchange revenue disappeared month-over-month.
3. **Segment/GL reconciliation** — we cannot trust operational segment data to manage the book.

I recommend an immediate deep-dive on the interest accrual process and the revenue drop before any capital or credit decisions.

beats.title: Round the table — CTO + CXO
beats.shows: the CEO consults the platform + experience seats; figures attributed
beats.question: Continue round the table. The CTO: is the platform healthy (reliability, deployments, incidents)? The CXO: how is the customer experience and what is the customer voice saying? Attribute every figure to the officer who gave it.
beats.answer:
Thank you, CTO. Thank you, CXO. Here is the rest of the table.

---

**CTO — platform health:**

The CTO reports the platform is **stable with one known blind spot**. Every deployment is healthy: **19 of 19 healthy, 0 degraded (100.00% healthy)** across both clusters. Crashloops: **none**. Restarts estate-wide total **32**, all low-count — the highest being `finance-mcp` and `modern-core` pods at **3 restarts each**, neither crashlooping.

Service self-reports are all green: `bank-api` (api ✓, database ✓), `coo` (ollama ✓, operations_mcp ✓, qdrant ✓), and `cfo` (ok). **Zero unhealthy, zero failing checks.**

On delivery: **19 rollouts complete, 0 progressing, 0 stalled**. No version drift. No active incidents — the prior `cfo` stalled-rollout incident remains **resolved**. The CTO took **no operator actions** because nothing qualified.

Three standing technical-debt items:
1. **`cfo` monitoring blind spot.** Its `/health` returns `ok` with an **empty checks map `{}`** — the only service with zero dependency probes. It would report healthy even with dependencies down, which masked the prior incident.
2. **Mutable image tags.** **13 of 16 apps (81.25%)** run on mutable tags (`dev` or `latest`), hurting traceability and safe rollback.
3. **No redundancy.** **17 of 19 deployments (89.47%)** are single-replica. One pod failure equals a service outage.

The CTO’s verdict: **stable, and not flying blind — with one exception.** Estate-wide signals are solid. The gap is narrow but real: for `cfo`, we rely on rollout/restart signals, not its health probe, to catch a recurrence.

---

**CXO — customer experience:**

The CXO reports the customer experience is dominated by a **severe onboarding blockage** and a **distressed customer-voice signal**, even though transaction-level friction remains low.

**Onboarding:** The funnel is completely blocked. There are **203 customers in the pipeline**, with **0 KYC completed** and a **KYC completion rate of 0.0%**. By contrast, existing accounts are fully activated — **458 active out of 458 total**, for an **account activation rate of 100.0%**.

**Engagement:** Over a **30-day window**, the bank has **203 total customers**, of whom **170 are active** and **33 are dormant**, yielding an **active rate of 83.74%** and a **dormant rate of 16.26%**. The CXO notes that with **0.0% KYC completion**, no new customers are entering the base, which is a structural attrition risk.

**Transaction friction:** Failure rates are **0.0%** across all products — payment (**1,150 total**), card (**2,228 total**), deposit (**86 total**), and unknown (**7,056 total**). Interac performance is strong: **772 completed out of 773 total** for a **completion rate of 99.87%**; there were **0 expired e-Transfers** and only **1 declined**.

**Product adoption:** Among **170 active customers**, card adoption is **74.71%** (**127 customers**), payment is **59.41%** (**101 customers**), and deposit is **29.41%** (**50 customers**). Deposit adoption is notably low.

**Customer voice — issues:** There are **40 open issues** and **0 resolved**. Top themes: **rail_experience (7 issues)**, tied with **onboarding (7 issues)**. Others: **app_ux (6)**, **declines_friction (5)**, **feature_request (4)**, **fees (4)**, and **other (7)**. By severity: **3 urgent**, **9 high**, **19 medium**, **9 low**. Three urgent personal-manager escalations are pending: an e-Transfer that expired before the payee claimed it, a request for recurring e-Transfers, and a customer who could not find the autodeposit setting.

**Survey signal:** The overall NPS campaign ("all_active") shows a score of **16**, based on **70 responses**: **31 promoters**, **19 passives**, and **20 detractors**. The CSAT campaign for the "has_open_issue" segment is critically low: **0.0% satisfied**, with **30 responses** and a **mean score of 1.77**. The CXO notes this indicates detractor clustering is likely concentrated among customers with unresolved issues.

**Ranked backlog:**
1. Unblock KYC onboarding — motivated by **203 customers at 0.0% KYC completion**, plus **7 onboarding issues** and **1 high-severity escalation**.
2. Resolve open-issue backlog — motivated by **40 open / 0 resolved**, **0.0% CSAT** in the has_open_issue segment (**mean 1.77**), and **3 urgent escalations**.
3. Improve rail experience and e-Transfer UX — motivated by **rail_experience being the top issue theme (7 issues)**, plus urgent escalations.
4. Boost deposit product adoption — motivated by deposit adoption at only **29.41%**.
5. Address app_ux discovery problems — motivated by **6 app_ux issues** and repeated escalations.

---

That completes the round. We now have the full cross-functional picture. Let me record the synthesis and determine next steps.

# Platform Health Review — point-in-time snapshot (right now)

**Verdict: STABLE — but with one known blind spot.** Everything I can see is green; the concern is that one service (`cfo`) can't fully see itself. Details below.

One caveat on framing: my reads are **point-in-time snapshots**, not windowed — I can tell you the state *right now*, not a 7-day trend.

## Reliability ✅
- **Deployments: 19/19 healthy, 0 degraded (100.00% healthy)** across both clusters (`nano-bank` + `modern-core`).
- **Crashloops: none.** The crashlooping list is empty.
- **Restarts: 32 total** estate-wide, all low-count. Highest: `finance-mcp-5d999f8f49-n57kx` (3) and `modern-core-659b5c4576-7m964` (3) — neither crashlooping.
- **Service self-reports: all healthy.** `bank-api` (api ✓, database ✓), `coo` (ollama ✓, operations_mcp ✓, qdrant ✓), `cfo` (ok). 0 unhealthy, 0 failing checks.

## Delivery / Deployments ✅
- **Rollouts: 19 complete, 0 progressing, 0 stalled.** Every deployment sits on a single active replicaset — no stuck or half-rolled revisions.
- **Version drift: none.** No app runs different tags in different places.

## Open incidents
**None active.** The prior `cfo` stalled-rollout/CrashLoopBackOff incident remains **resolved** — I deep-dived it: `cfo` is 1/1 ready/available, rollout complete on one active replicaset, pod `cfo-c97f58d78-52dlb` at 0 restarts, no drift.

## Operator actions
**None taken — nothing qualified.** No deployment was crashlooping/unready (restart precondition) and no rollout was stalled with a healthy prior revision (rollback precondition). The bank verifies these live; there was nothing to act on.

## Technical debt — 3 standing items (persistent risks, not live faults)
1. **`cfo` monitoring blind spot (the important one).** Its `/health` returns `ok` with an **empty checks map `{}`** — it's the *only* service with zero dependency probes. It would report "healthy" even with its dependencies down — exactly what masked the prior incident. **Recommend adding real dependency probes.** I can delegate this as a scoped, PR-gated remediation to the engineering coder (human reviews and merges) if you want it actioned.

The gap is narrow but real: `cfo`'s self-report is liveness-only, so for that one service we'd rely on rollout/restart signals — not its health probe — to catch a recurrence. Fix the `cfo` probes and the "blind spot" caveat goes away.

## NANO-BANK EXECUTIVE BRIEF — STATE OF THE BANK

**Period:** September 2026 close / current week  
**Sources:** CFO (books), COO (operations), CTO (platform), CXO (customer experience)

---

### TOP CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PRIORITIES

**1. Restore interest income — the NIM engine is dead.**  
The CFO reports NIM for September 2026 was **0E-25**, effectively **0%**, on average earning assets of **CAD 8,294,115.63**. The CFO also reports NIM was **2.10%** in July 2026 and collapsed to **0%** in August 2026, where it has remained for two consecutive months. Interest income and interest expense are both booked at zero despite carrying **CAD 8,000,001.00** in loans receivable. This is the single biggest driver of the profitability decline and must be treated as a P0.

**2. Unblock KYC onboarding.**  
The CXO reports **203 customers in the pipeline**, with **0 KYC completed** and a **KYC completion rate of 0.0%**. No new customers are entering the base. This is a structural growth and attrition risk that sits at the intersection of product, compliance, and engineering.

**3. Resolve the open customer-issue backlog.**  
The CXO reports **40 open issues** and **0 resolved**. CSAT in the "has_open_issue" segment is **0.0%** satisfied with a **mean score of 1.77** across **30 responses**. The NPS campaign ("all_active") shows a score of **16**, based on **70 responses**: **31 promoters**, **19 passives**, and **20 detractors**. Unresolved issues are poisoning the customer voice and concentrating detractors.

**4. Fix the Lynx recall pattern.**  
The COO reports the Lynx rail over 30 days shows **4 recalled** out of **16 total Lynx items** by count, and **$4,399,756.24 recalled** out of **$14,855,863.95** total Lynx volume by value. The COO also reports a **$15,000.00 rejected** Lynx wire in the 30-day window. This is a money-movement integrity issue that threatens counterparty trust and operational stability.

**5. Remediate the CFO monitoring blind spot.**  
The CTO reports the `cfo` service `/health` returns `ok=true` with an **empty checks map `{}`** — the only service with no dependency probes. It would report healthy even during a stalled rollout or dependency failure, which masked the prior incident. This is a platform-observability gap that directly affects financial reporting reliability.

---

### TOP CROSS-FUNCTIONAL RISKS

**1. Capital is at razor-thin levels and deteriorating.**  
The CFO reports the leverage ratio for September 2026 was **0.102112141**, or approximately **0.10%**, and the risk-weighted capital ratio was **0.153611761**, or approximately **0.15%** — far below any prudential standard. Total equity is **CAD 1,515,656.15** (comprising **CAD 1,500,000.00** in capital and **CAD 15,656.15** in current earnings) against **CAD 14,843,055.22** in total assets. Economic capital is **CAD 986,679.76** and total risk-weighted assets are **CAD 9,866,797.55**. RAROC is **-0.111073178**, or **-11.11%** annualized, with risk-adjusted economic profit of **-CAD 109,593.66** annualized. The expected credit loss for the period was **CAD 10,654.14**, which exceeds the period's net income of **CAD 1,646.44** by **CAD 9,007.70** — the expected loss is roughly 6.5 times the reported net income. The CFO notes the ledger books no loan-loss provision, so headline ROA/ROE look better than true economics.

**2. Revenue has halved and the income model is broken.**  
The CFO reports net income for September 2026 was **CAD 1,646.44**, down from **CAD 3,292.88** in August 2026 — a 50% drop month-over-month. ROA annualized fell from **0.27%** to **0.135%**; ROE from **2.58%** to **1.34%**. With NIM at zero and fee revenue collapsing, the bank has no sustainable earnings engine.

**3. Customer balance stress is showing in card declines.**

The 30-day NSF rate eased slightly to **0.09649837133550489** (approximately **9.65%**), but declines remain heavily concentrated in NSF on the card_authorize channel, with **237 NSF declines totaling $1,073,963.96** over 30 days. This signals deposit-base fragility that feeds back into credit and liquidity risk.

**4. Platform resilience is brittle under the surface.**  
The CTO reports **19 of 19 deployments healthy (100.00%)** with **0 degraded**, and **0 pods crashlooping**. However, **17 of 19 deployments** (every app deployment except coredns) run at **desired = 1** (single replica) — a single pod failure is a service outage. Additionally, most app services run the mutable **`dev`** tag and `qdrant` runs **`latest`**, hurting traceability and safe rollback. While all rollouts are currently complete with none stalled, the architecture is not fault-tolerant.

**5. Segment and GL data cannot be trusted for decision-making.**  
The CFO reports September 2026 segment reporting shows only one operating segment, `card|payments`, with income of **CAD 801.94** and net income of **CAD 801.94**. However, segment net income of **CAD 801.94** is **CAD 844.50** below the GL net income of **CAD 1,646.44**, corresponding to Fee Income that appears in the GL but not in the segment tables. The CFO also notes that in August 2026, the segment variance was **CAD -4,848.12**. Until this variance is explained, the segment data is not reliable for P&L or value-creation analysis.

**6. Deposit product adoption is weak, constraining funding diversification.**  
The CXO reports deposit adoption among active customers is only **29.41%** (**50 of 170**). With the loan-to-deposit ratio at **5.96** per the CFO, the bank is funding loans largely through non-deposit liabilities. Low deposit adoption amplifies funding and liquidity risk.

**7. The AFT rail carries unresolved technical concerns.**  
The COO reports the 30-day AFT rail shows **6 rejected entries ($243.00)** against **37 settled ($407,700.72)**, and while the 7-day window was clean with **0 exceptions**, the prior batch-accumulator blockage remains an unresolved technical concern should outbound AFT volume resume.

---

### BOTTOM LINE

Nano-bank is in a critical cross-functional squeeze: **zero NIM, halved fee revenue, ~10-bps capital, a Lynx recall rate of roughly 25% by count and ~30% by value, 0% KYC completion, 40 unresolved customer issues, and a platform that is green today but one pod failure away from outage.** The bank is pre-provision profitable but economically loss-making. No single function owns this — it requires coordinated action across finance, operations, platform, and customer experience.

**Next step:** I will determine which acting-officer directives are warranted and which require observation and recommendation only.
